known_relevant_issue_records.title: Complete deferred source-qualified curation in final unmatched review shards
known_relevant_issue_records.body:
Final coordinator review of two published source-review shards found that several no-change outcomes defer already-authorized curation rather than identify a missing scientific fact. Worker04 head `0d2c73e5aee5adb88782537755472d9ca0c5c3cd`; worker08 head `7efd3f8b98f9e822431dcb510c2c242a2569cfc7`; both depend on #1158 at `e000d66`.

Concrete examples:

- Worker08 case `CM_NAME:b9a945a3356d0c885eea986a2f6223e78c8e7d7163ee95629061a640294cbbe8` (H2O deionized) correctly distinguishes deionization from distillation, but its remaining requirement is to perform native owner lookup and use or create the appropriately scoped owner. [DSMZ533](https://www.dsmz.de/microorganisms/medium/pdf/DSMZ_Medium533.pdf) explicitly identifies deionized water in both main and trace stock. No proposal or completed lookup disposition accompanies that deferred step.
- Worker08 case `CM_NAME:e69128522cfe555f63dd51d4a23ece86363290b3839180386b090f368b28d1cc` (glycine-NaOH buffer) preserves a source-defined concentration and pH, and correctly finds a receiving-medium volume transcription error. [JCM906](https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=906) specifies the separately prepared buffer. The decision defers representing the stock without explaining which missing fact prevents a bounded preparation identity. It must not be equated to pure glycine or assigned invented titrant amounts.
- Worker04 case `CM_NAME:2f91fab8feab468a33e48d01e2f0a1363b9ad70816766c69a1e8d68c0ed6f8d5` describes the [NBRC15](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=15) treated, clarified V-8 preparation but defers representing it until later curation. Lack of a molecular mapping or extraction yield does not by itself establish that a source-qualified preparation cannot be represented with an honest partial assertion.

Related outcomes defer normality-qualified NaOH stocks, source-specific top layers, C9322 supplied-form review, and malted wheat meal because an exact molecular/ontology mapping or later complete-owner review is absent. These are leads for reassessment, not predetermined identity approvals. Genuine solvent, formulation, provenance or supplied-form uncertainties may remain after primary research.

Reassess the full no-change cohorts against MAPPING_SEMANTICS sections3/6 and add-media. Complete supported proposal work, or state the precise scientific fact still missing and the actual primary-source searches. Keep receiving-medium dose/unit repair separate from ingredient identity. Never invent concentrations, solvent, chemistry, product equivalence, component completeness, or exact ontology matches; preserve all native holds and old review bytes. Require separate skeptical review of successor evidence/payloads and ordinary commits/pushes on the existing worker branches. No maintained data or export approval is requested from workers.

This extends the same class of completeness problem seen in #1163 and #1193 to distinct final shards; those earlier findings remain preserved. Exact frozen decisions and capture hashes are retained in the coordinator's immutable `w04-w08-deferred-curation-v1/review-inputs.json` and will accompany the campaign evidence. This is a review-completeness finding, not a statement that every listed source must map.

known_relevant_issue_records.title: Complete source-defined worker05 formulation curation before final shard acceptance
known_relevant_issue_records.body:
Worker05's published source-review head `b44430c9230e62f9d9d73154484311b77442e73e` declares the shard complete, but at least one no-change disposition defers curation that the campaign already authorizes rather than documenting an unavailable scientific prerequisite.

Affected case: `KG_CASE:b58f2778ba8c8905faf5cddf634ff4d5059978baa1b2489af2eb4db7f7e9fef1`, MediaDive ingredient1382, Grace's Insect Medium. Existing source owner: `data/ingredients/unmapped/Graces_Insect_Medium.yaml`, SHA256 `98d818debe40f93d28b7c08b2a7437b6a3c8566e12c857aa7f42fd3c1cdafa3e`.

The [committed decision](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/b44430c9230e62f9d9d73154484311b77442e73e/reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-05/media/decisions.json) explicitly binds the source to Sigma G8142 and cites the manufacturer's complete formula. Its no-change and missing-requirement fields say to curate that formula and review component identities. There is no proposal, and no distinct missing evidence for the whole supplied product is identified.

The [manufacturer formula](https://www.sigmaaldrich.cn/deepweb/assets/sigmaaldrich/product/documents/172/423/g8142for.pdf) distinguishes G8142 liquid1x from G9771 powder, including bicarbonate treatment. Worker evidence `MEDIA-SIGMA-G8142-FORMULA` retains the PDF at SHA256 `7a07a208abd686522d82c3d61bc682af4e377ebd226bdbe786c2f9e84727b140`. This is a lead for supplied-product curation, not approval of any generic medium equivalence or every component identity.

MAPPING_SEMANTICS sections3 and6 and the add-media workflow distinguish whole preparation identity from component grounding. Named ungrounded parts may remain explicit; a missing component CURIE is not by itself proof that an evidence-defined preparation must stay entirely uncurated. The campaign requires justified curation, not only a list of future curation tasks.

Please reassess this case and the other worker05 no-change dispositions whose stated blocker is simply to curate, define or reconcile an already identified formulation. For each, either prepare a concrete evidence-backed proposal through the existing proposal workflow, or record the exact unresolved scientific fact and the primary-source searches actually attempted. Preserve historical/source scope, competing-owner boundaries, raw labels, prior holds, and separate full-payload/release review. Do not invent a catalog variant, infer a complete formula from a source name, merge owners, treat all product names as resolved, or approve roles.

For G8142 specifically, verify the source-to-product attribution and all current owner occurrences before choosing whether the existing owner can be specialized or a separate source-qualified preparation is needed. Transcribe only supported formulation claims; preserve any uncertainty in individual component form or quantity explicitly. Independent re-review must cover the revised disposition/proposal and final head.

Deduplication: the complete652-visible-issue all-state snapshot and relevant Grace/G8142/worker05 title/body matches contained no exact completeness finding. #1176 and #1177 cover separate peptone/Sea Salts defects. This issue does not reopen those or supersede a scientific hold.

known_relevant_issue_records.body:
Worker04 found four source defects that need upstream reconciliation before source-specific matching can be released. This MIM tracking issue records the integration blockers; it does not authorize changing CultureMech from this worker.

All four current CultureMech `main` files were read through GitHub on 2026-11-08 at 05:13–05:21 UTC and matched the frozen case bytes. Captures, hashes and primary references are retained in `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-04/captures/current-issue-owners/` on branch `review/all-unmatched-w04-source-review-20261107`.

| Source record | Observed conflict | Required follow-up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data/normalized_yaml/algae/merds_my75s.yaml` | Ingredient `Thoroughly disperse the agar in cold`, with75%w/v, is a preparation-sentence fragment. The [CCAP MErds/MY75S sheet](https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_MErds_MY75S.pdf) describes a biphasic medium with separate recipes and stock bases. The normalized two-ingredient record is not a faithful reconstruction. | Remove the phantom token while reconstructing the entire phase/stock structure and preparation instructions from the source; do not treat75% seawater as75% agar or just delete one row. |
| `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/isosphaera_medium.yaml` | `Agar, Noble (BD214050), if needed` combines Noble grade with a catalog number that [BD identifies as Bacto Agar](https://www.bdbiosciences.com/en-ca/products/reagents/dehydrated-culture-media/agars/agar-bottle-100g.214050?tab=product_details). [Noble Agar214220](https://www.bd.com/en-us/products-and-solutions/products/product-page.214220) is a different product. | Recover the original ATCC recipe/version or procurement evidence and decide which field was wrong. Retain the contradictory raw label until resolved. |
| `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/JCM_J1429_M1H_NAG_ASW.yaml` | Free N-acetyl-D-glucosamine is annotated CHEBI:8006 (peptidoglycan context), while [JCM1429](https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1429) lists the free ingredient, consistent with CHEBI:506227. | Correct the upstream monomer grounding with primary recipe and ontology evidence. The MIM spelling proposal must not conceal this upstream error. |
| `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/aam.yaml` | The record calls its source AAM-minus but includes D-glutamate1.71mM. [Lee2009](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2698402/) Table4 row13 gives L-glutamic acid250mg for AAM; the Methods explicitly omit L-glutamic acid from AAM-minus. | Reconstruct the intended AAM/AAM-minus variant and stereochemistry, rather than changing D to L alone. Do not extend this correction to the separate Klein1979 occurrences without their original methods. |

Related, but different, work: CultureMech#408 concerns TOGO volume-to-g/L normalization; the closed CultureMech#273 parsing correction concerned SBBM, not this CCAP MErds/MY75S record. MIM#587 concerns KG instructional labels; its comments retract blanket parenthetical filtering. These four findings need source-specific fixes, not generic label stripping.

Acceptance: each corrected source cites its original evidence, preserves recipe variants and supplied forms, gets independent source review, and is then reconciled with frozen MIM case IDs and holds during the coordinator's integration. No maintained file or export has been changed by worker04. Campaign dependency #1158 and publication holds #1157 remain active.

Deduplication searched the complete retrieved MIM and CultureMech issue/PR title/body inventories plus relevant prior comments. No exact open task for these four records was found within that bounded search; this is not a claim that every historical comment was searched.

known_relevant_issue_records.title: Reject the disodium EDTA alias on the trisodium EDTA owner
known_relevant_issue_records.body:
`data/ingredients/mapped/Na3-edta.yaml` correctly denotes CHEBI:63125 EDTA trisodium salt but contains the active exact synonym `EDTA di sodium salt`. This makes a two-sodium label resolve to a three-sodium substance.

The owner was checked against live `main` on 2026-11-08 at 05:13 UTC and matches the frozen worker04 baseline, SHA256 `ea8dbade6d6bfd0bbb478bd146a1266dbb2742c7d022a3de16904465ea73238a`. [CHEBI:63125](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:63125) is trisodium; disodium EDTA and its dihydrate are distinct CHEBI:64734 and CHEBI:64758 identities. Worker04's `3Na-EDTA` case includes three original recipe occurrences whose sodium count agrees with the trisodium owner.

Worker04 proposes exact isolated owner bytes that retain the incorrect disodium string as `REJECTED_LABEL`, add the supported `3Na-EDTA` spelling, and append a curation-history event. The maintained owner and exports remain unchanged until coordinator integration. This does not resolve other EDTA hydrate/duplicate-owner conflicts and does not approve unrelated existing aliases or the complete published payload.

Acceptance: the disodium string no longer resolves as an active trisodium alias; source provenance remains visible; the three source occurrences retain their original amounts and stock context; coordinator reconciliation uses the original before hash and new complete-payload review before any export release.

Frozen case `CM_NAME:02591f4a5364db919b1a8890e8f6800a87eea943fff102ed0405d0de9b069fa5`; proposal `w04-chem-proposal-trisodium-edta`. Exact payload and evidence are under `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-04/` on branch `review/all-unmatched-w04-source-review-20261107` (dependency #1158). Full current issue/PR title/body search found no matching open task; this remains under the broader #1157 publication hold.

known_relevant_issue_records.title: Reconcile Mg-citrate 1:1 source evidence with the 3:2 owner before source release
known_relevant_issue_records.body:
Worker04's frozen source review found a stoichiometry conflict that should be resolved by tracing source occurrences before changing the whole owner.

`data/ingredients/mapped/Mg-citrate.yaml` denotes CHEBI:131391 trimagnesium dicitrate / CAS 3344-18-1, but retains 1:1 magnesium-citrate properties and synonyms. Its exact bytes were checked against live `main` on 2026-11-08 at 05:13 UTC and match the assigned frozen baseline (SHA256 `6601f382062758877609574deeb7a2d72d9f0c6d693139b55ac031cfc6e2fb1f`).

[MediaDive ingredient404](https://mediadive.dsmz.de/ingredients/404) exposes CAS144-23-0, formula C6H6MgO7 and molecular weight214.413. The frozen source record's g/L-to-mM conversion agrees with that 1:1 representation. [CHEBI:131389](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:131389) and [CHEBI:131391](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:131391) distinguish 1:1 magnesium hydrogen citrate from 3:2 trimagnesium dicitrate. MediaDive's automatic metadata and derived conversion are mutually consistent, but are not independent procurement evidence.

The prior #320 decision and #353 implementation deliberately selected 3:2 using a name-preprocessed CAS. That history must remain visible. One later source record is insufficient to reverse all five occurrences represented by the owner.

Proposed follow-up:

- Trace all five owner occurrences to original recipes and supplier/CAS/form evidence, distinguishing observed reagent identity from automatic database enrichment.
- Propose a source-bound split or a fully justified reground. Reconcile identifier, ontology, CAS, formula, mass and aliases together; retain rejected provenance.
- Withdraw inherited complete-payload support for changed owners and run guarded synchronization, SSSOM and native complete-payload review at integration.

No owner change or hold release is proposed in worker04 for this case. Frozen case: `KG_CASE:6fd10b406feae9b043de0cb1b917ea47ac39dd6157b4170e26daab2fd5600a20`. Evidence, full prior comments and independent review are in `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-04/` on branch `review/all-unmatched-w04-source-review-20261107` (campaign dependency #1158; coordinator integration pending).

Deduplication checked all current MIM issue/PR titles and bodies before filing; #320/#353 are historical context, not a currently open source404 split task. This finding does not supersede the campaign-wide publication hold in #1157.

known_relevant_issue_records.title: Prevent retired placeholder reuse in the #914 hydrate split records
known_relevant_issue_records.body:
The approved replacement of #914 exposed a historical identifier collision in its two new hydrate placeholders. `scripts/fix_merge_tombstone_resolution.py` assigns `UNMAPPED_0819` to Na2moo4_X_H2o and `UNMAPPED_0820` to Trisodium_Citrate_X_3_H2o.

Both identifiers already occur in committed historical records: `git show 5b993ad7:data/ingredients/unmapped/Hydroxystreptomycin.yaml` starts with UNMAPPED_0819, and the Isophthalate record at that revision starts with UNMAPPED_0820. A search including ignored backups also found earlier uses. Their absence among active current identifiers is insufficient: the manage-identifiers skill explicitly forbids reuse of retired placeholders.

Before the replacement PR is published, allocate two unused identifiers after checking current records, ignored artifacts and history; update the guarded writer, new records and assertions together, retaining the original port provenance and appending an audit event. Add a regression that prevents these retired IDs from being assigned to the new substances. Regenerate exports and unified mapping and run native QC. This is a routine safety correction within the approved #882/#914 port, not a scientific identity decision.

| 6643131b (#802, 2026-10-05) | 47 | 9,391 |
| 1742bfd4 (#863, 2026-10-12) | 33 | 3,378 |

kg-microbe's consolidator skips REJECTED rows (`scripts/consolidate_chemical_mappings.py:1604-1606` at kg-microbe 1408e7099). MIM therefore supplies no identity for these labels. I did not check what kg-microbe falls back to.

## Cause

claw's unified builder finds a merge tombstone's target in `_mim_merge_target` (`scripts/build_unified_ingredient_mapping.py:129-140` at the pinned claw a5d56296):

```python
for event in reversed(data.get('curation_history', []) or []):
    if event.get('action') in MIM_MERGE_ACTIONS:
        return (data.get('identifier') or '').strip()
    if event.get('new_status') == 'REJECTED':
        return ''
```

The builder walks the history backwards and stops at the first event with `new_status: REJECTED`. Nine tombstones later gained a bookkeeping event recorded as REJECTED → REJECTED, so the walk stops before it reaches the merge:

| tombstone | identifier | blocking event |
|---|---|---|
| `Cocl2_X_6_H2o` | CHEBI:53503 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Na2moo42h2o` | CHEBI:75213 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Calcium_Chloride` | CHEBI:3312 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Sodium_Citrate` | CHEBI:32142 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o` | CHEBI:32142 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Na-glutamate` | CHEBI:64243 | REJECTED_WRONG_FORM_SYNONYMS (#757) |
| `Mgcl2x_6_H2o` | CHEBI:86345 | CORRECTED (#739) |
| `Nah2po4h2o` | CHEBI:114249 | CORRECTED (#755) |
| `Cinnamic_Acid` | CHEBI:35697 | CORRECTED (#755); none of the 33 rows |

The corpus has 81 REJECTED records. Of these, 13 set `representative:`, 51 resolve through their merge event, these 9 resolve to nothing, and 8 have no merge event. The #755 CORRECTED events were written "so the merged name is credited to the live record". In the unified build they have the opposite effect.

## Rows affected

| labels | occurrences | identity at 48408270 | answer the records support now |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` | 2,317 | CHEBI:53503 cobalt chloride hexahydrate | same |
| 7 other CoCl2·6H2O spellings | 358 | CHEBI:35696 cobalt dichloride (anhydrous) | CHEBI:53503 |
| 6 Na2MoO4·2H2O spellings | 412 | CHEBI:75213 sodium molybdate dihydrate | same |
| 5 Na2MoO4·H2O spellings | 8 | CHEBI:75215 sodium molybdate (anhydrous) | none: no monohydrate record |
| `Sodium citrate`, `Sodium Citrate`, `sodium citrate` | 94 | CHEBI:53258 sodium citrate | contested, see below |
| `Calcium chloride`, `calcium chloride` | 82 | CHEBI:86158 calcium chloride dihydrate | CHEBI:3312 (live `CaCl2` lists `Calcium chloride`) |
| `Calcium Chloride` | 15 | CHEBI:3312 calcium dichloride | same |
| `Trisodium citrate x 2 H2O`, `Trisodium citrate・2H2O` | 77 | CHEBI:53258 sodium citrate | CHEBI:32142 sodium citrate dihydrate |
| `Trisodium citrate・3H2O`, `Trisodium citrate x 3 H2O` | 3 | CHEBI:53258 | none: no record for that form |
| `NaH2PO4•H2O` | 4 | CHEBI:37585 sodium dihydrogenphosphate (anhydrous) | CHEBI:114249 monohydrate |
| `MgCl2x 6 H2O` | 4 | CHEBI:86345 magnesium dichloride hexahydrate | same |
| `MgCl2 x 7H2O` | 2 | CHEBI:6636 magnesium dichloride (anhydrous) | kgmicrobe.compound:mgcl2_x_7_h2o |
| `Na-glutamate` | 2 | CHEBI:64220 monosodium glutamate | CHEBI:64243 monosodium L-glutamate |

- **Rows that lost an identity the records still support:** 2,748 occurrences in the "same" rows, mostly `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` (2,317) and the sodium molybdate dihydrate spellings (412).
- **Rows that had a wrong form at 48408270:** 534 occurrences. These should have been corrected, not dropped.
- **Contested labels (94 occurrences):** for the sodium citrate names, live `Trisodium citrate` (CHEBI:53258) lists `Sodium citrate`, while live `Na3-citrate x 2 H2O` (CHEBI:32142, the dihydrate) lists `Sodium Citrate`.
- **`Na-glutamate` (2 occurrences):** it had generic monosodium glutamate, where MIM now holds the L-form.

## Fix

Setting `representative:` on the nine tombstones, as 13 others already do, would make claw resolve them again. That step alone is not safe. Several tombstones still carry names of other forms as publishable synonyms, and a restored merge target would publish those names under the wrong form:

- `Cocl2_X_6_H2o` (hexahydrate): `CoCl2 x 2 H2O` and `CoCl2 x 4 H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM). Both forms have had their own records since #863.
- `Na2moo42h2o` (dihydrate): four monohydrate spellings (HYDRATE_FORM): `Na2MoO4 . H2O`, `Na2MoO4 · H2O`, `Na2MoO4.H2O` and `Na2MoO4xH2O`.
- `Mgcl2x_6_H2o` (hexahydrate): five spellings, `MgCl2 x 7 H2O`, `MgCl2 x 7H2O`, `MgCl2x7H2O`, `MgCl2  x 7 H2O` and `MgCl2  x 76 H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM).
- `Trisodium_Citrate_X_2_H2o` (dihydrate): `Trisodium citrate·3H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM).
- `Calcium_Chloride` (anhydrous): `CaCl22H2O` (HYDRATE_FORM). #757 retyped two other dihydrate spellings but not this one.
- `Na-glutamate` (monosodium L-glutamate): `(2S)-2-aminopentanedioate` and `L-glutamic acid dianion` (EXACT_SYNONYM). Both are names of the anion.
- `Sodium_Citrate` (dihydrate CHEBI:32142): its preferred term `Sodium Citrate` is a generic name, and its synonym `Na2citrate` names disodium citrate.

Suggested order:

1. Retype those names as REJECTED_LABEL, or move each to the record for its form, with curation events.
2. Set `representative:` on the nine tombstones. If review pins (#740, #745) block these edits, change claw instead: when looking for the merge, skip events whose `previous_status` is already REJECTED.
3. Rebuild with `just rebuild-unified`. Check that the 33 rows come back, except the 11 occurrences whose form has no record.
4. Add a gate. `check-unified-freshness` and `check-unified-rejections` both pass on the current snapshot. Either of these checks would have caught this:
   - every merge tombstone carries `representative:`;
   - no REJECTED row without an identity has a tombstone's name as its label.

Related:
- #878 covers MAPPED labels that sit on a different hydrate.
- #877 is the membership rebuild. It reports that CultureMech#591 now refuses tombstone redirects across hydrates on CultureMech's side.

## Correction to #863

#863's description calls rows like these "merged-tombstone answers that the reviewed builder withholds (MIM #811, #816)". Nothing is withheld on purpose: the builder loses the merge target as described above, and neither #811 nor #816 covers that.

known_relevant_issue_records.title: Sodium glutamate・H2O has a correct record (CHEBI:232425) but resolves to nothing
known_relevant_issue_records.body:
Found by the #624 rebuild in #653.

Before the rebuild, the surface form `Sodium glutamate・H2O` resolved to `CHEBI:64220` — the **anhydrous** `Na glutamate` record. MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 refuses that, so the rebuild correctly stops matching it, and the row is now `UNMAPPED`:

```
Sodium glutamate・H2O	4	(chebi_id, cas_rn, kg_microbe_node_id, mim_id all empty)	UNMAPPED
```

But a **correct record already exists**:

```
data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_Glutamate_Monohydrate.yaml
  identifier: CHEBI:232425
  preferred_term: Sodium glutamate monohydrate
  mapping_status: MAPPED
```

So the substance is curated and the name still goes nowhere — 4 CultureMech occurrences that had a wrong answer now have none.

**Why it misses:** an ignore-inclusive search (`rg -uu`) finds the surface form in no record at all, and the monohydrate record's synonym list carries no hydrate-notation variant:

```
sodium (2S)-2-azaniumylpentanedioate, Glutamate Sodium, Glutamate monosodium salt,
Glutamic acid monosodium salt, Glutammato monosodico, L(+) Sodium glutamate, MSG,
Monosodioglutammato, Natrium L-hydrogenglutamat, Natriumglutaminat,
Sodium hydrogen glutamate, sodium (2S)-2-ammoniopentanedioate
```

Nothing there matches `Sodium glutamate・H2O`, and the separator is U+30FB KATAKANA MIDDLE DOT — the same non-ASCII hydrate notation that shows up elsewhere in this corpus (`(NH4)6Mo7O24・4H2O`).

**Fix:** add the hydrate surface form as a synonym on `Sodium_Glutamate_Monohydrate.yaml` with a `curation_history` event. Worth checking the other `・`-separated forms for the same shape while in there — this is #251's family (hydrate notation hidden in synonyms) seen from the other side.

Not a blocker for #653: the rebuild is a strict improvement over resolving a hydrate to its anhydrous parent.

known_relevant_issue_records.title: Triage the 71 records asserting a mapping their own research report advised against
known_relevant_issue_records.body:
## Finding

`scripts/validate_records_against_research.py` (#309) compares each ingredient
record against the deep-research report for that same ingredient. Over the 527
records researched so far it found **71 `STATUS_CONFLICT`s** — the record asserts
an ontology mapping while its own report recommended `UNMAPPED`.

**Every one of them was written by the same mechanical sweep,
`promote_resolved_unmapped`.** That is the #203/#263 pattern recurring: a
plausible identifier promoted by a mechanism that never decided anything.

## Important caveat — do not treat all 71 as defects

The Edison/PaperQA3 lane cannot open an ontology page. Its reports say so
verbatim ("no ChEBI CURIE was verified in the retrieved evidence"), so it
defaults to "retain UNMAPPED" whenever it cannot confirm a term — which is most
of the time. An Edison "retain UNMAPPED" on its own is therefore weak evidence.

That is exactly why the second (Claude) lane exists, and it already resolved 22
of these: `LANE_DISAGREEMENT_RESOLVED` marks a conflict the Claude lane cleared
by resolving the term Edison could not. Those 22 need no action.

## Triage order

Work `mappings/record_research_validation.md`, most severe first:

1. **17 `BOTH_LANES_DISPUTE`** — both independent lanes dispute the mapping.
   Strongest signal in the ledger; start here.
2. **`P1 CURIE_REFUTED`** — a report names the record's exact CURIE and argues
   against it. The quoted line usually names the right term.
3. **`P1 VERDICT_REFUTES`** — a per-field verdict table refutes an identity
   field and supplies a corrected value.
4. The remainder of the `STATUS_CONFLICT`s, checking `promoted_by` and
   `documented_rationale`.

Each row carries the quoted report line that produced it, so most are a one-read
decision: keep with a written justification, downgrade `mapping_quality`, or
demote.

## Note on coverage

The ledger currently covers 527 of 2,841 records; the Edison sweep is ongoing
(~30 records/hour, account-capped). Re-run the validator as it completes — these
counts will grow.

disposition: No genuinely new independent maintained-data finding established by this successor review. Deferred work is already issue1201; Mg/EDTA/source conflicts and Middlebrook remain1190/1191/1192/1173. #655 prior glutamate recommendation is explicitly reassessed, not silently adopted; #312 remains. Draft duplicate/payload/provenance defects were corrected before publication and do not warrant duplicate repository issues.
limits: Searches cover exact retrieved titles/bodies, not unqueried comments. Specific agent issue captures document any additional comment inspection. Other-shard work is not claimed reviewed.
